hero.title: Virtual Eco-Explorer: Exploring the Boundaries of the Puger Ecosystem
hero.description: Behind the crashing waves and the mesmerizing sunsets of Puger Beach, lies a hidden secret that threatens our future. Through 360° exploration videos and augmented reality technology, let's go beyond the limits of sight to uncover how microplastic pollution infiltrates the food chain and affects human health. This beauty is ours, and so is our responsibility to protect it.

objectives.title: Learning Objectives
objectives.goal_1: Students are able to analyze socio-scientific issues related to microplastic contamination in the Jember region and its systemic impacts on public health and the ecosystem
objectives.goal_2: Students are able to evaluate the complexity of the problems at the Puger Fish Farm by integrating ecological (pollution), economic (the welfare of fishermen and traders), and social (community behavior) aspects
objectives.goal_3: Students are able to propose strategic and innovative solutions for microplastic mitigation that consider the balance of ecological, economic, and social aspects in a sustainable manner in the Jember region
objectives.goal_4: Students are able to demonstrate systems thinking and sustainable awareness in making logical decisions in everyday life

mission.title: The Invisible Crisis
mission.subtitle: Microplastics in the Jember Ecosystem
mission.description: A multidisciplinary investigation into how urban plastic consumption patterns create a systemic threat extending 45 km to the Puger estuary.

context.p1: The problem begins when people's consumption patterns change There has been a drastic shift to single-use plastics, while the waste management system has not been able to keep up with the load. Plastic waste dumped into the <0>Bedadung River</0> in urban areas doesn't stay there.
context.p2: The river carries it 45 km to the Puger estuary. There, invisible particles infiltrate <0>the tissues of fish and shellfish</0>, posing a systemic threat to public health and the balance of Jember's interconnected ecosystem.

goal.title: Module Objective
goal.desc: Dissect this system from the <0>human behavior</0> level to the <1>fish cellular level</1>. Are you ready to begin your investigation?

signin.label: Researcher Identifier (ID)

initial.instruction: Watch a 360° video of the port and interviews with three stakeholders (Seafarers, Seafood Vendors, and Government Officials).

tips.suffix: For a full 360° experience, click and drag the video screen to look around the TPI and see the perspectives of different stakeholders.

sailor.label: Fishermen
sailor.summary: Complaining about piles of trash caught in their nets and boat engines.

seller.label: Seafood Seller
seller.summary: Concerned about the quality of fish contaminated by plastic waste at the port.

official.label: Government Official
official.summary: Explaining the difficulties of waste management regulations in coastal areas.

initial.issue_description: After watching the video and listening to the interview, what are the most pressing issues? Why are these issues interconnected between fishermen, fish sellers, and the government?

component_id.title: Identifying Ecosystem Components
component_id.description: Identify at least 5 components (biotic and abiotic). Use the table feature to group them: Components, Types, and Roles (Source of Pollutant/Victim/Medium of Transportation).

table_component.role_placeholder: Source of Pollutant, Victim, Medium of Transportation

properties.title: Component Interaction Analysis
properties.description: Choose one plastic and one organism, then analyze their properties and predict their interactions.

plastic_form.title: Plastic Component
plastic_form.props_placeholder: Does it float? What size is it? Is it difficult to biodegrade?
plastic_form.behave_placeholder: How does this property facilitate its entry into the food chain?

organism_form.title: Organism Component
organism_form.props_placeholder: How does it feed? Where does it live?
organism_form.behave_placeholder: Why do the biological properties of this organism make it vulnerable to Component A?

initial.footer: Ensure all component and property observations are filled in before proceeding to the analysis phase.

qualitative.instruction: Compare the large plastic bottles (seen at the port) with the microplastic fibers (mentioned by the seller).

analysis.q1_desc: If plastic waste (such as drinking bottles or fishing nets) were in Puger waters for a very long time, what would most likely happen to the shape and size of the plastic? Explain the factors that influence these changes!
analysis.q2_desc: Based on their shape, microplastics are divided into several types. Explain the differences in shape and state the main sources of plastic!
analysis.q3_desc: Observe the following two organisms that live in Jember waters: the Blood Clam (Anadara granosa), which is a filter feeder (filters water) at the bottom of the waters, and the Tuna, which is an active predator in the waters. Why is the Blood Clam Are tuna at higher risk of exposure to microplastic fragments that settle on the seabed than tuna? How do the differences in their "feeding habits" determine the types of microplastics that enter their bodies?

qualitative.footer: This qualitative analysis will form the basis for quantitative calculations in the next phase.

quantitative.instruction: Pay attention to the data table on the abundance of microplastics in various areas in Jember from rivers to beaches.

questions.q1_desc: Why does concentration drop at Station 4 but spike at Station 3? Link this to river runoff vs ocean currents.
questions.q2_desc: Based on Station 2, estimate particles ingested if a human drinks 2L of water/day.
questions.q3_desc: Calculate BMF between Cockles and Tuna. If a person eats 250g of cockles/week, how many mg of plastic is ingested?

placeholders.q1: Explain the interaction between runoff and currents...

explanation.instruction: Open the Augmented Reality (AR) app on your device. Focus on the "Cellular Impact" and "Fragmentation" modules.
explanation.q1: Use your observations from the AR tool to explain the mechanism problem.
explanation.q2: How can a plastic bottle from the harbor (seafarer's domain) physically transform into a health risk for consumers (seller's domain)?
explanation.q3: Create a mechanism diagram using arrows and your explanation should consider chemical interactions in various subsystems, such as the atmosphere, the air column, and biological cells.

decision.instruction: You are a consultant to a government official. You must propose a strategy to reduce microplastic levels (e.g., a “Microfilter Act” for washing machines or a “Plastic Tax”).

labels.social_impact_desc: Social Impact of the Seafaring Community

questions.conclusion_desc: Why is this systemic solution more effective than just a professional-scale 'Beach Cleanup'?

placeholders.general: Impact analysis from a consultant's perspective...
placeholders.final: Synthesis of why upstream prevention is better than downstream cleanup...

reflection.instruction: Compose a short reflection that summarizes the following points.
reflection.insight_desc: What profound knowledge has stuck with you most (for example: the mechanism of plastic fragmentation or the impact of pesticides on nerves)?
reflection.feel_desc: How did you feel (angry, sad, challenged, or inspired) after realizing that Jember's natural beauty harbors a serious health threat?
reflection.teach_desc: As a prospective educator, how has this experience of learning using immersive technology (AR & 360°) influenced the way you want to teach your students in the future? Do you feel this method is more capable of building environmental stewardship?
reflection.action_desc: How has this learning strengthened your desire to contribute to preserving the earth, starting with small steps in the Jember environment?
